blocks.content: Local self-government is the administration of local affairs by local bodies representing local inhabitants, ensuring democratic decentralization at the grassroots level.

items: Lord Ripon is hailed as the 'Father of Local Self-Government in India'.
Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) was the first to recommend democratic decentralization through a 3-tier Panchayati Raj system.
73rd Amendment added Part IX and the 11th Schedule (29 subjects), while 74th Amendment added Part IX-A and the 12th Schedule (18 subjects).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Local Self-Government refers to the management of local affairs by elected local representative bodies possessing substantial autonomy.
Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882 is historically recognized as the 'Magna Carta' of local self-government in India.
Article 40 of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) directs the State to organize village panchayats as units of self-government.
The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts of 1992 conferred constitutional status on rural (Panchayats) and urban (Municipalities) local bodies.
